name: GS-IR
definition: GS-IR is an inverse rendering approach based on 3D Gaussian Splatting that leverages forward mapping volume rendering to achieve photorealistic novel view synthesis and relighting results, estimating scene geometry, surface material, and environment illumination from multi-view images captured under unknown lighting conditions.
summary: GS-IR is an inverse rendering method using 3D Gaussian Splatting to estimate geometry, materials, and lighting from multi-view images, offering real-time efficiency and handling occlusion via baking.
